prelude.note: the overview, as Newbury's: high over the post-end bend, looking up the course with the stands on one side and the festival on the other

view.lede: The Ring, right-handed: one of the five generic courses that every course without its own build races on for now (very tight, near-circular), with the smaller of its two stand sides. A tight stadium oval of about 1m½f with a short run-in (about 1½f): no straight course, the sprints go round, chutes for the 6f, 7f and the long trips. Dressed as a suburban park.
notes: About 8.4f round, a 1.4f run-in. Drawn from a few numbers (the corners and bends of the loop, the chutes), so it can be reshaped quickly.
Suburban park: old small stands and pavilions clustered round the winning post, near the end of the straight, the crowd up to the rail, the festival in the infield opposite.
Choose Medium or Low under Quality in the race view's bar. Auto steps down by itself.
